ai.description: Cnemaspis australis is a small gecko reaching 40 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include keeled ventral scales and a slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis australis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale vertebral stripe and a lack of enlarged, spine-like tubercles on its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis australis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces and tree trunks at mid-to-high altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Southern Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt small insects on granite outcrops and rocky surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis australis* is oviparous, typically laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season and post-monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis australis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
